# Novel immunotherapy for canine lymphoma

This is an example listing generated for demonstration purposes. It is not a real recruiting study.

Interventional · Oncology · Investigator: Dr Sarah Mitchell

Canine

## Study overview

This prospective multi-centre study evaluates a novel monoclonal antibody immunotherapy for dogs with newly diagnosed B-cell lymphoma. The trial aims to improve remission rates and quality of life compared with standard chemotherapy protocols. Participating centres across England and Scotland will enrol eligible dogs following confirmation of diagnosis by cytology or histopathology. Owners receive full disclosure of risks, benefits, and alternative treatment options before consent.

## Condition

Lymphoma

## Study title

Engaging the Immune System to Kill Solid Tumors in Pet Dogs - A Comparative Oncology Approach (TriKE + Radiation Therapy)

## Purpose of study

The purpose of the study is to identify a safe and effective dose of a novel immunotherapy drug (TriKE) when given with hypofractionated radiation therapy (RT) in companion dogs with a sarcoma. 

## Eligibility criteria

Dogs must: 

  * Have cytologically or histopathologicaly confirmed sarcoma, measuring at least 2cm
  * Weigh at least 7 kg (15 lbs)
  * Modified performance score less than 2 and expected survival of at least 2 months

In people, the intestinal microbiome has emerged as a key modulator of cancer biology, influencing tumor development, host immune function, treatment response, toxicity profiles, and overall patient outcomes. # NEOVACC

  * #### Research type

Targeting Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer with Doggybone Personalised Cancer DNA Vaccines (dbPCV)

  * #### Research summary

Personalised cancer vaccines (PCV) are a new approach for training a person’s immune system to attack the cancer. In this trial for patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), each person receives a unique vaccine, made from their own genetic information (DNA), called a doggybone vaccine . We will add the vaccine to a common therapy for NSCLC, a drug called pembrolizumab. Pembrolizumab is used on its own to treat NSCLC if at least 50% of the cancer cells show a molecule called PDL1 (programmed-death ligand 1). Pembrolizumab is given for up to 2 years but may be stopped early if it does not work or if it causes side effects that make it unsafe to continue.

# NHS Cancer Vaccine Launch Pad

The NHS Cancer Vaccine Launch Pad (CVLP) is a platform that will speed up access to messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) personalised cancer vaccine and other immunotherapy clinical trials for people who have been diagnosed with cancer. It will also accelerate the development of cancer vaccines and other immunotherapies as a form of cancer treatment.

Through the CVLP, people with cancer who are receiving treatment in the NHS in England can be assessed to see if they might be eligible to join a cancer vaccine or other immunotherapy clinical trial, and then referred to a hospital that is running that trial.

This collaboration, initially with pharmaceutical company BioNTech, is a significant step towards realising the potential of new and innovative immunotherapy treatments, including these personalised cancer vaccines, in cancer treatment, in the hope of transforming patient outcomes in the future.

Over time, the CVLP will enable patients to access multiple trials running in different NHS trusts in other parts of the country, increasing access in an equitable way.

PRECINCT 2022 Goals

The PRECINCT 2022 teams are investigating diverse immunotherapies in dogs: checkpoint inhibitor, cytokine, vaccine, oncolytic virus, and adoptive CAR-iNKT cell therapies. The U01 and U24 investigators, DCTD staff, NCI intramural Comparative Oncology Program staff, and a wide range of canine cancer researchers who are funded from sources inside and outside the network attend monthly PRECINCT steering committee meetings. The network’s goals are to:

  * Support canine clinical studies using immunotherapeutic agents and novel therapeutic combinations together with laboratory correlative studies. These studies will seek to describe, characterize, and understand the cellular and molecular mechanisms that determine the anti-tumor response (or non-response) in dogs with spontaneous tumors
  * Include laboratories and canine clinical trial sites that will share therapeutic agents, specimens, and laboratory and clinical protocols to standardize and validate the data generated
  * Support submission of canine data to the Integrated Canine Data Commons
